columns.name: VulnTitle
values: Apache HTTP Server HTTP/2 Denial of Service Vulnerability (CVE-2024-38476)
Microsoft Windows SMB Server Remote Code Execution Vulnerability (CVE-2024-21351)
SSL/TLS Server Supports TLSv1.0 and TLSv1.1
SSL/TLS Server Supports Weak Cipher Suites
Linux Kernel netfilter Local Privilege Escalation (CVE-2024-1086)
Microsoft Exchange Server ProxyShell Multiple Vulnerabilities
Microsoft Windows Remote Desktop Services Remote Code Execution (CVE-2024-43533)
Microsoft Windows Cumulative Security Update Missing
VMware ESXi OpenSLP Remote Code Execution (CVE-2021-21974)
Citrix ADC and Gateway Remote Code Execution (CVE-2023-3519)
Fortinet FortiOS SSL-VPN Heap Buffer Overflow (CVE-2024-21762)

columns.name: Solution
values: Upgrade OpenSSL to version 3.0.13, 3.1.5, or 3.2.1 or later as recommended by the vendor.
Apply Apache HTTP Server 2.4.62 or later. Refer to the Apache security advisory for affected versions.
Install the latest cumulative security update for Microsoft Windows. See KB5034768 for details.
Update the Linux kernel to the patched version supplied by your distribution and reboot.
Apply the Microsoft Exchange Server cumulative update and security update for ProxyShell.
Upgrade Apache Log4j to version 2.17.1 or later. Remove the JndiLookup class as a temporary mitigation.
Upgrade OpenSSH to 9.8p1 or later, or apply your distribution's backported patches for CVE-2024-6387.
Apply the latest Microsoft monthly security update addressing CVE-2024-43533.
Upgrade runc to 1.1.12 or later and Docker Engine to 25.0.2 or later.
Apply VMware ESXi patch ESXi70U1c-17325551 or later. Disable OpenSLP service if patching is not possible.
Upgrade Atlassian Confluence Server/Data Center to version 7.18.1 or later.
Upgrade Citrix ADC/Gateway to firmware build 13.1-49.13 or later.
Apply the Progress MOVEit Transfer hotfix released June 2023 or later.
Upgrade Fortinet FortiOS to 7.4.3, 7.2.7, 7.0.14 or later.
Apply the Ivanti Connect Secure / Policy Secure mitigation XML and patch when available.
Renew the expired SSL/TLS certificate with a CA-signed certificate.
Disable TLSv1.0 and TLSv1.1 on the affected service. Enable only TLSv1.2 and TLSv1.3.
Replace the self-signed certificate with one issued by a trusted certificate authority.
Configure Redis with `requirepass` and bind only to trusted interfaces.

columns.name: Consequence
values: A remote attacker could execute arbitrary code on the affected system, leading to full system compromise.
Successful exploitation could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code with the privileges of the affected service.
Successful exploitation could lead to denial of service, allowing an attacker to crash the system or cause it to become unresponsive.
A local attacker could escalate privileges to root and gain complete control of the system.
An authenticated attacker could execute arbitrary code with SYSTEM privileges on the Exchange server.
An attacker could fully compromise the host via crafted JNDI lookup strings, leading to remote code execution and lateral movement.
Sensitive information may be disclosed to a man-in-the-middle attacker who can intercept and decrypt communications.
Container escape could allow an attacker to gain root access on the underlying host.
Exposes the service to credential brute force attacks and unauthorized data access.
Allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to bypass authentication and access protected resources.

columns.name: Diagnosis
values: QID detected the affected version of OpenSSL is installed on the host. The version reported is vulnerable to the referenced CVEs.
The Apache HTTP Server version banner indicates a release prior to the patched build addressing this vulnerability.
The host is missing one or more cumulative security updates from Microsoft. Patch level analysis indicates the system is vulnerable.
The Linux kernel version reported by the system is vulnerable to a known privilege escalation flaw.
Microsoft Exchange Server build number indicates the server is missing the cumulative update addressing the vulnerability chain.
A vulnerable version of the Log4j library was detected in one or more application directories on the host.
OpenSSH server banner reports a version known to be vulnerable to the referenced CVE.
TLS handshake negotiation succeeded with TLSv1.0 and/or TLSv1.1, which are deprecated and considered insecure.
The SSL certificate presented by the server is self-signed and not issued by a trusted certificate authority.
The Redis service is accessible without authentication on the network.
The Docker Engine version installed on the host is vulnerable to a known runc container escape flaw.
